subject: tinRobot
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: wind-up robot with key in its back.
Style: 1950s Japanese tin toy.
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module for a 1950s-style Japanese tin wind-up robot toy—humanoid, with a back key and a rigged skeleton—thinking through realistic scale, settling on roughly 0.25-0.3 meters tall to match a real toy's proportions.

Now I'm sketching the classic tin-robot aesthetic: a boxy, slightly tapered body with lithographed chest dials, a grill mouth, dome head with antenna, round eyes, cylindrical arms with claw hands, and flat boxy feet, finished with rivets and stripes in red, cream, teal, and chrome. I'm mapping out the skeleton hierarchy—hips, spine, neck, head with hinged jaw, shoulders through fingertip joints, legs down to ankles, plus a separate hinge joint for the two-lobed brass wind-up key and the antenna.

Setting up the import statements for the clockwork and glow kits...

I'm continuing to plan out dimensions for the legs, torso, neck, and head, deciding where the antenna sits on top to bring the total height to roughly 0.32m, then moving into the joint hierarchy -- defining a hip root joint and a spine chain running from hips up to the neck base.

Now I'm placing the neck and head joints, choosing a forward-facing direction for the head to simplify local orientation, then adding a jaw joint beneath it for a hinge-style mouth movement. I'm also starting to lay out the shoulder and elbow joint positions for the arms, scaled by the side multiplier.

I'm settling on an A-pose for the rest pose, angling the arms outward from the shoulders through elbows to wrists so the limbs stay separated from the torso, then I'm moving on to define claw-style finger joints for the hands.

For the legs I'm placing hip, knee, and ankle joints down the leg chain with a contact point at the ankle, then adding a key joint hinged at the back of the chest and a simple antenna joint at the top of the head. Now I'm working out the torso geometry, planning to build it as a tapered frustum shape running from waist to shoulder.

For the surface look, I'm designing a lithographed tin-toy paint style with a noisy red base, plus a textured chest panel using an SVG decal with dials, gauges, rivets, and retro text like "ATOMIC," along with a separate circular gauge texture and small riveted studs around the torso edges.

Then I'm planning out the rest of the body construction: cylindrical shoulder caps with rivets, segmented arm rods with ribbed bands, clawed hands built from curved box sections swept along bezier paths, boxy striped legs with cylindrical knee joints, and feet made from boxes with a toe-plate decal, leading into head construction.

Now I'm detailing the head design—a boxy shape with a visor, lens-style glowing eyes using concentric SVG rings, a grilled jaw with glowing vertical bars, and ear knobs with an antenna. For the back-mounted key accessory, I'm wrestling with how to extrude a figure-eight outline since a simple extrude can't create holes, so I need another approach for that shape.

Writing key extrude geometry...

I'm also sketching in a brass wind-up key with flat shading, a back panel decal reading "MADE IN JAPAN" for authenticity, and considering adding a small visible gear train behind a belly window for extra mechanical detail.

Now I'm defining the paint palette — red, cream, and teal tin colors with worn/chipped shading, plus chrome and brass metal finishes, and setting up striped lithograph patterns for the legs.

Switching to a crisper custom paint approach for the tin lithography instead of noisy stripes, using a helper function that shades and adds scratch highlights to a base color via mix and noise utilities from the SDK. Writing tin paint helper...

I'm planning out the texture set needed: chest panel litho, glowing eye lens, mouth grill lights, back plate branding, foot stripes, gauge and gear textures, and shoulder star decal—around eight total. Then I start sketching the builder setup, defining the hip joint as the root of the robot's skeleton.

Building the spine chain...

Still refining head dimensions...

Antenna topped with a glowing red ball plus small disc. For the color scheme, I'm settling on red body, teal-blue litho head, chrome steel arms, red legs with cream stripes, teal feet with red toe plates, brass key, and yellow eyes.

Now I'm building the torso as a frustum shape tapering from waist to shoulder width, skinned across the spine bone chain, with a cream chest panel plane positioned on the front face where the body's depth curve places it.

Since the front face slants, I need the panel to sit flush against it rather than floating in front, so I'm computing the face normal from the slope between waist and shoulder depth, then offsetting the panel point along that normal for a snug fit. I'm weighing whether a simpler straight-sided torso box would avoid this complexity, but tapering reads better visually, so I'll just build a reusable helper to compute the front-face position and normal at any height for placing decorations.

Now I'm sketching the chest layout: paired chrome dial knobs near the top, a lithograph panel centered below them, and a gear-filled porthole lower down, trying to work out exact coordinates and sizes so nothing overlaps.

Computing the gear pitch radii and placement relative to the porthole, I realize the gears would be hidden behind the solid torso face unless the porthole is actually cut as a hole rather than just a ring overlay — I need to rework the porthole geometry so it's a real opening.

Still working out gear positioning...

Also need to assign the gear spin bone — spine1's joint range fits around y=0.152, so I'll attach spin there with two joints added, keeping default tints since flat gear style doesn't need custom ones.

I'm adding a dark backing disc behind the gears and nudging gear depth placement forward so the back faces don't render toward the viewer and collide with the disc — gears get centered a bit further out, plus a brass rim torus around the assembly.

Now I'm working on the key joint at the back: a brass rod shaft extending outward with a collar, then building the key head as an extruded shape with a rounded bow and two D-shaped holes, oriented so the head plane contains the shaft axis with lobes sticking out sideways.

Still shaping key outline...

I'm adding a textured backplate with "MADE IN JAPAN" lettering below the key, then designing shoulder joints with riveted cylinder caps in red tin. For the arms, I'm giving them a ribbed accordion look using a wavy radius function along the tube, mimicking classic tin robot joints in chrome steel.

Writing arm sweep code...

I'm placing a red ball joint at the elbow and a cylindrical cuff at the wrist, then starting on claw-like hands with articulated thumb and finger digits.

Defining thumb and finger joints with chrome sweep geometry for the claw tips, then setting up the leg chain from hip to knee to ankle with appropriate widths relative to the torso.

Now I'm shaping the upper and lower leg segments as tapered frustum boxes with striped litho paint, adding a chrome cylinder joint at the knee, and considering how to handle the hip joint where it meets the torso. I'm sketching a paint function that stripes the leg based on vertical position.

For feet, I'm placing a teal tin box geometry at the ankle bone with flat shading, plus a toe plate decal and a chrome bumper rod along the front bottom edge, then adding a vertical ankle cuff cylinder to bridge the foot and leg cleanly.

Writing rivet helper function... Now I'm setting up a rivet helper that merges small spheres into a flat-colored chrome mesh, placing them along the torso's four corner edges by computing the half-width and half-depth profile at each height.

Continuing with the neck cylinder and ring, then head details: a cream brow plate, side vents, a mouth grill, and shoulder star decals using circle geometry oriented along the shoulder cap axes, plus a teal paint job for the head with a lithographed panel.

Now I'm sketching SVG textures: a cream chest panel with red border stripes, two dials with tick marks and red needles, colored light rectangles, and lightning bolt accents; an eye texture with concentric yellow and orange rings plus a white highlight and glow; and a mouth grill with dark plate and cream vertical bars glowing teal.

I'm also planning smaller SVGs for the back litho text ("MADE IN JAPAN", "WIND-UP ROBOT"), a toe plate with diagonal stripes, and a star badge, then setting up helper constants for waist and shoulder proportions to compute body widths.

Still writing helper functions...

Continuing with the pelvis block under the torso, shoulder cap cylinders that protrude beyond the torso width, and defining arm joint positions for shoulder and elbow attachment points.

Checking arm segment lengths from shoulder to elbow to wrist, confirming adequate clearance from the torso, then sweeping a chrome accordion-style tube along the arm chain with flat caps so the shoulder cap and wrist cuff conceal the joints.

Adding the elbow joint ball and wrist cuff cylinder...

Still placing the key geometry...

Now I'm adding an antenna joint at the top of the head, with a base disc, a thin rod, a glowing red ball tip, and a small mid-ring.

Then I'm working out the skull box dimensions relative to eye placement, the jaw section below it with its hinge joint and front mouth grill, and the small gap separating jaw from neck cylinder to keep proportions consistent.

I'm adding a cream brow strip above the eyes for a visor-like look, plus darker side vents on the head, and placing cylindrical ears jutting from the sides sized to fit the head's half-width. Then I start figuring out the chest geometry by interpolating a parameter along its height curve.

Next I'm positioning front-facing dial knobs with chrome bodies and red caps at the chest plane, then writing a helper function that merges small rivet spheres into a single geometry attached to a bone for efficiency.

I'm placing torso rivets in rows along the frustum edges tied to the chest spine bone, then adding head rivets along the top front edge, and starting on foot rivet placement.

For texturing, I'm skipping decals since flat painted planes already cover the surface needs, and I'm deciding against panelled seams on the feet since the geometry's too small for a 2.5mm seam. I'm planning glow effects for the eye lenses, mouth grill, and antenna ball, but leaving the gauge non-glowing, while the chest panel keeps its own distinct color scheme.

For the leg litho, I'm writing a paint function that cycles red, cream, and a thin dark ink line based on vertical position. I'm also placing a toe plate plane on the foot's top face, working out the correct orientation vectors so it faces forward rather than degenerating from a parallel direction.

Now I'm positioning the back plate, computing its normal vector from the slope of the back surface so it sits flush. Then I'm sketching an SVG chest panel with a cream background, red border frame, and dark dial circles outlined in a lighter tone.

Still writing SVG code...

I'm also double-checking API details like glow/clockwork import paths, the flat-normals option, offset/lerp helpers, and how to chain the arm joints to the spine for the robot rig.

Now I'm working through the leg construction using frustum boxes for the hip-to-knee and knee-to-foot segments, adding litho color accents, and verifying the gear train's position, axis, and bone bindings are correctly specified.

Checking gear spoke calculations for the small 12-tooth gear against the rim-minus-hub threshold confirms no spokes are needed, so I can keep the gear fields minimal — just a flat two-gear setup with an arbor, totaling a manageable part count.

With module settled at 0.0012, thickness comes out to 0.0024, and I'm positioning gears slightly offset from the face. I'm verifying that gearTrain accepts a Joint for its bone reference, confirming frustumBox is available, and now moving to writing SVG helper functions before the final code assembly, including the meta export. I still need to double check eye glow textures, the jaw joint's aim direction, skip pelvis rivets, compute claw offsets using a unit vector between two points, and confirm rgb is properly exported from the paint module.

Writing tin paint shader...

Still figuring out side panel placement and geometry, then I need to be careful with TypeScript strict mode rejecting unused imports or variables as I write the final code.

Writing the imports and setting up the Three.js vector math...

Generating tick marks and rivet colors...

Now I'm adding the shoulder cap geometry with a star emblem on the outer end, plus red arm band rings positioned along the upper and lower arm using lerped points between joints.

Moving to the lower body, I'm placing toe bumpers on the feet, building the pelvis block with hip knobs on the sides, and adding a chrome belt piece across the hips.
